basic_identification.full_title: Portable Solid Bio-Mass Cookstove (Chulha) — Specification (First Revision) (सुवाह्य ठोस बायो-मास कुकस्टोव (चूल्हा) — fof'kf"V (पहला पुनरीक्षण))
basic_identification.sector_category: Mechanical Engineering / Non-Conventional Energy Sources (finalized by the Bio-mass Cookstove Panel, MED 04:2/P-1, and approved by the Non-Conventional Energy Sources Sectional Committee, MED 04, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This Indian Standard prescribes the materials, constructional designs, dimensions, safety profiles, thermal efficiency performance standards, emission limits (CO and CO2), and testing protocols for portable solid bio-mass cookstoves (commonly known as chulhas) designed for domestic, commercial, or institutional cooking.

allied_standards.title: Composite Bottom for Stainless Steel Cooking Utensils — Specification
allied_standards.relevance: Provides baseline parameters for multi-layered cooking pots. The cookstove thermal efficiency test uses standard aluminium vessels which correspond directly to the heat-conducting characteristics of composite bottoms.

allied_standards.title: Code of Practice on Occupational Safety and Health Audit
allied_standards.relevance: Directs safety audits in industrial manufacturing yards where sheet metal pressing, high-temperature cast iron pouring, and battery assembly present mechanical and electrical hazards.

allied_standards.title: Occupational Health and Safety Management System
allied_standards.relevance: Unifies risk mitigation, requiring regular safety check logs of hyperbaric, combustion, and mechanical systems.

allied_standards.title: Code of Practice for General Steel Construction
allied_standards.relevance: The master structural steel code in India, regulating support steelwork, hangers, and structural columns carrying overhead exhaust hoods and chimneys in institutional kitchens.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Mechanical Engineering Department / Non-Conventional Energy Sources)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). However, portable cookstoves (chulhas) must hold a valid BIS license to print the physical 'ISI Mark' standard mark on the stove outer shell to be eligible for government subsidies, carbon-credit certifications, rural development funding, and public procurement tenders managed by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Government of India.

requirements.detail: Portable cookstoves must be structurally fabricated from high-durability metals. Typical designs utilize structured legs, insulated handles, a combustion chamber (minimum 1.6 mm thick), a outer jacket (minimum 1.0 mm thick), and a bottom plate (minimum 2.0 mm thick) to prevent structural sag under load.

Forced-draft cookstoves (Design 'C') must incorporate a battery-powered fan blower, a variable-speed potentiometer control, a secondary air manifold with secondary air holes, and a variable height grate to optimize air-to-fuel ratios.

Prescribes standard test vessel dimensions and water loads based on the cookstove's rated heat input rate (e.g., Sl No. i: up to 2000 kcal/h utilizes an 180 mm diameter x 100 mm height aluminium vessel carrying 2.0 kg of water; Sl No. xxiii: 15401 to 16400 kcal/h utilizes a 510 mm diameter x 275 mm height vessel carrying 44.00 kg of water).

The thermal efficiency calculation utilizes specific heat constants for both water (Cw = 4.186 kJ/kg/°C) and the aluminium testing vessel (Cv = 0.896 kJ/kg/°C). Thermal efficiency (η) is calculated using the ratio of heat utilized (Hout) to heat produced (Hin).

During CO and CO2 emissions testing, the stainless steel sampling probe must be positioned perpendicular to the flue gas flow inside the exhaust duct, placed at a minimum of five pipe diameters downstream of any flow disturbances.

Verifies the durability of cast iron components. The cookstove is burnt at its rated fuel rate for 45 minutes (feeding fuel at 1/4th of the burning rate every 15 minutes). The cast iron components are immediately de-linked from the hot stove and quenched in cold water, requiring the water to be changed after every immersion. The component must show zero cracking or structural failure.

All observed or calculated test and performance values (including thermal efficiency, dimensions, and emissions) must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 13152 (Part 1) : 2013 (First Revision) is the primary national Indian Standard specification establishing technical, structural, thermal, and environmental requirements for portable solid bio-mass cookstoves (commonly known as chulhas). Maintained under the Non-Conventional Energy Sources Sectional Committee (MED 04) and reaffirmed in 2024, the standard unifies requirements for both natural-draft and forced-draft (fan-assisted) cookstove designs. To support public health, clean cooking, and forest conservation in rural areas, the standard enforces strict thermal efficiency calculations (utilizing standard specific heats of water and aluminium vessels), prescribes precise vessel and water quantities for performance testing, regulates exhaust flue gas sampling (requiring probe placement at least five pipe diameters downstream of flow disturbances), and mandates a severe thermal-shock quench test on cast iron components to prevent structural cracking under rapid cooling.
